title: Name the structure
note: A functional group is the part of a molecule that sets how it reacts. In these skeletal drawings each corner or line end is a carbon carrying enough hydrogens to make four bonds; only heteroatoms and their hydrogens are written.

items.ex: A carbon-carbon double bond, R₂C=CR₂; names end in -ene.
A carbon-carbon triple bond, RC≡CR, linear at each sp carbon; names end in -yne.
An aromatic benzene-type ring: six carbons drawn with alternating double bonds.
R–X, a halogen (F, Cl, Br, or I) bonded to an sp³ carbon.
R–OH, a hydroxyl group on an sp³ carbon; names end in -ol.
R–O–R′, one oxygen bonded to two carbons.
R–SH, the sulfur analog of an alcohol; names end in -thiol.
RNH₂, R₂NH, or R₃N: nitrogen single-bonded to carbon, with no carbonyl attached.
RCHO, a carbonyl carbon bonded to at least one hydrogen; names end in -al.
RCOR′, a carbonyl carbon bonded to two carbons; names end in -one.
RCOOH, a carbonyl bonded to a hydroxyl group; names end in -oic acid.
RCOOR′, a carbonyl bonded to an oxygen that carries a carbon; names end in -oate.
RCONR₂, a carbonyl bonded to nitrogen; names end in -amide.
RCOCl, a carbonyl bonded to chlorine; names end in -oyl chloride.
RCO–O–COR′, two acyl groups sharing one oxygen; names end in -oic anhydride.
R–C≡N, a carbon triple-bonded to nitrogen; names end in -nitrile.
A strained three-membered ring of two carbons and one oxygen: a cyclic ether.
R₂C=NR, a carbon-nitrogen double bond, also called a Schiff base.
Ar–OH, a hydroxyl bonded directly to an aromatic ring; far more acidic than an alcohol (pKa about 10).
R–S–R′, the sulfur analog of an ether; also called a thioether.
R–S–S–R′, formed by oxidizing two thiols; disulfide bridges hold many proteins in shape.
RCOSR′, an ester with sulfur in place of the single-bonded oxygen; acetyl CoA is one.

title: Groups in real molecules
note: Real molecules carry several functional groups at once, and each one reacts in its own way. Find the highlighted atoms, decide whether a carbonyl is involved, and check what sits on each side of it.

items.ex: Aspirin's –COOH makes it an acid; it is acetylsalicylic acid.
The acetyl ester: a C=O whose carbon is also bonded to an O that leads to the ring.
The benzene ring is the aromatic core of aspirin.
The OH sits directly on the ring, so it is a phenol, not an alcohol.
N bonded to a carbonyl carbon is an amide, not an amine.
The carbonyl carbon carries an H, which makes it an aldehyde.
The methoxy group, ring–O–CH₃: an oxygen between two carbons with no C=O.
Vanillin is 4-hydroxy-3-methoxybenzaldehyde; the 4-OH is a phenol.
The C=C between the ring and the aldehyde is a trans alkene.
Cinnamaldehyde gives cinnamon its flavor.
Benzocaine is ethyl 4-aminobenzoate, an ethyl ester.
An NH₂ on the ring with no carbonyl beside it is an amine (an aniline).
The carbonyl carbon is bonded to two carbons, so it is a ketone.
Raspberry ketone is 4-(4-hydroxyphenyl)butan-2-one.
Every standard amino acid has an amine on the α-carbon, next to the carboxyl group.
Alanine is drawn here in its neutral form; in water near pH 7 it exists as a zwitterion.
